payload.rationale: The Federal Reserve recently raised the target range by 25 basis points in September 2026 to 3.75-4.00% (a midpoint of 3.875%). The September Summary of Economic Projections indicates a median end-2026 federal-funds midpoint of 4.1%, which implies one additional 25 bps hike over the two remaining meetings in 2026 (October and December). The Fed often prefers to space out rate hikes to assess incoming data, making a pause (0 bps hike) in October plausible, reserving the final hike for December. However, the probability could be too high if upcoming inflation data remains elevated, prompting the FOMC to hike at consecutive meetings. Conversely, the probability could be too low if the Fed's standard practice of waiting for December's SEP meeting to adjust rates strongly dictates a pause in October.
limitations: Year-end dot projections do not identify which meeting will contain an adjustment; two scheduled meetings remain after September.
New inflation and employment information before October 28 can change policy.
